from_quote: before the adoption of this Conſtitution, ſhall be as valid againſt the United States under this Conſtitution, as under the Confederation.
rationale: The paragraph prints Article VI, Clause 1 of the Constitution as signed; the quoted words are the same as the clause's (apart from capitals and the long s), though the pamphlet's punctuation differs in places.
to_quote: before the Adoption of this Constitution, shall be as valid against the United States under this Constitution, as under the Confederation.

from_quote: and all treaties made, or which ſhall be made, under the authority of the United States, ſhall be the ſupreme law of the land; and the Judges in every State ſhall be bound thereby
rationale: The paragraph prints Article VI, Clause 2 of the Constitution as signed; the quoted words are the same as the clause's (apart from capitals and the long s), though the pamphlet's punctuation differs in places.
to_quote: and all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby

from_quote: The Senators and Repreſentatives before mentioned, and the members of the ſeveral State Legiſlatures, and all executive and judicial officers, both of the United States and of the ſeveral States, ſhall be bound by oath or affirmation, to ſupport this Conſtitution; but no religious teſt ſhall ever be required as a qualification to any office or public truſt under the United States.
rationale: The paragraph prints Article VI, Clause 3 of the Constitution as signed; the quoted words are the same as the clause's (apart from capitals and the long s), though the pamphlet's punctuation differs in places.
to_quote: The Senators and Representatives before mentioned, and the Members of the several State Legislatures, and all executive and judicial Officers, both of the United States and of the several States, shall be bound by Oath or Affirmation, to support this Constitution; but no religious Test shall ever be required as a Qualification to any Office or public Trust under the United States.

from_quote: THAT treaties ſhould be the ſupreme law of the land is warmly oppoſed by the enemies of the Conſtitution
rationale: The paragraph takes up the objection that treaties should be "the supreme law of the land," the words of Article VI, Clause 2.
to_quote: all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land

from_quote: TREATIES ought of right to be conſidered in the light
rationale: The paragraph defends the Convention's view of treaties, as stated in the clause printed above it (Article VI, Clause 2).
to_quote: all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States

from_quote: The article reſpecting the habeas corpus act corroborates this doctrine
rationale: The paragraph cites "the article respecting the habeas corpus act" and says it may be suspended when circumstances require, which is Article I, Section 9, Clause 2.
to_quote: The Privilege of the Writ of Habeas Corpus shall not be suspended

from_quote: But ſtill there are fears for the diſtrict which may become the ſeat of Congreſs, and which may be ten miles ſquare
rationale: The paragraph speaks of fears for "the district which may become the seat of Congress, and which may be ten miles square," the district of Article I, Section 8, Clause 17.
to_quote: over such District (not exceeding ten Miles square)

from_quote: the Conſtitution has not only guaranteed to them a republican form
rationale: The paragraph says the Constitution "has guaranteed to them a republican form," which refers to Article IV, Section 4.
to_quote: The United States shall guarantee to every State in this Union a Republican Form of Government
